title: Standardization of a new non-invasive device for assessment of arterial stiffness in rats: Correlation with age-related arteries’ structure
author: Fabricio, Jordão, et al.
materials: test-retest of rater A on Experiment 1;
test-retest of rater B on Experiment 1;
test-retest of rater A on Experiment 2;
test-retest of rater B on Experiment 2;

steps.title: House and weigh animals
steps.instruction: Keep rats in a temperature‑controlled room (22 ± 2 °C) with a 12/12 h light/dark cycle, provide food and water ad libitum, and measure body weight of each conscious animal before any anesthesia.

steps.title: Anesthetize for PWV measurement
steps.instruction: Inject each rat intraperitoneally with xylazine hydrochloride 10 mg kg⁻¹ and ketamine hydrochloride 50 mg kg⁻¹ (Vetbrands).

steps.title: Position pOpet probes and set conditions
steps.instruction: Place two pOpet® probes (Axelife SAS, France) on the right forelimb (near the elbow) and right hindlimb (near the knee). Position the photodiode (signal receiver) on the dorsal side of each limb and the infrared LED on the ventral side. Maintain the room at 22 °C, a heating plate at 43‑45 °C, and keep the rat’s core temperature at 37 ± 1 °C. Ensure a quiet environment and avoid intense ambient light.

steps.title: Measure inter‑probe distance
steps.instruction: Using a flexible tape measure, record the linear distance (D) between the two photodiodes in centimeters (cm).

steps.title: Record transit time and calculate PWV
steps.instruction: After the signal stabilises, turn off the heating pad and record the transit time (TT) for 10 seconds with the pOpet® 1.0 software. Perform ten consecutive measurements on the same animal and compute the average TT (in seconds). Calculate pulse‑wave velocity (PWV) with the formula PWV (m s⁻¹) = D (m) / TT (s).

substeps.instruction: Repeat the measurement ten times per rat.
Convert D from cm to meters before calculation.

steps.title: Validate non‑invasive PWV invasively
steps.instruction: In two rats (n = 2), catheterise the carotid and femoral arteries, record arterial pressure waveforms simultaneously, and compute the delta time between pressure pulses. Compare this invasive delta time (s) with the TT (ms) obtained from the pOpet® device. After recording, euthanise the rats, excise the aorta and iliac arteries, and measure their lengths; confirm that these lengths match the tape‑measured D used for calibration.

steps.title: Test‑retest and inter‑rater consistency
steps.instruction: For internal consistency, perform ten measurements, then remove both photodiodes, disconnect the device from power, wait 2 minutes, reconnect the probes and power, and repeat ten measurements on the same rat (same‑day test‑retest). Repeat the entire sequence on the following day. Have two independent researchers (Rater A and Rater B) perform the same protocol on each day to assess inter‑rater reliability.

substeps.instruction: Day 1 – Rater A: test‑retest (steps 1‑10, disconnect, wait 2 min, repeat).
Day 1 – Rater B: same as above.

steps.title: Collect arterial tissue (Study 2)
steps.instruction: Twenty‑four hours after PWV assessment, deeply anaesthetise rats with xylazine 20 mg kg⁻¹ and ketamine 160 mg kg⁻¹ (IP). Perform a ventral midline thoracic incision, then transcardiac perfusion with ~100 mL sterile saline followed by ~200 mL 4 % paraformaldehyde in buffered PBS (0.1 mol L⁻¹ phosphate buffer, pH 7.2) at a flow rate of 20‑30 mL min⁻¹ using a peristaltic Milan pump. Harvest ~5 mm segments of descending thoracic aorta, femoral artery and common carotid artery (5 rats per age group).

steps.title: Fix, dehydrate and embed tissues
steps.instruction: Fix the harvested segments for 24 h in 4 % buffered paraformaldehyde (0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.2). Dehydrate through graded ethanol series (70 %, 80 %, 90 %, 100 %). Embed tissues in histological paraplast.

steps.title: Section and mount for histology
steps.instruction: Cut transverse sections 10 µm thick with a microtome. Mount 10‑15 sections per slide on glass slides.

steps.title: Stain for smooth muscle and elastic fibers
steps.instruction: Stain selected sections with hematoxylin‑eosin (H&E) to visualise smooth‑muscle constituents, and with Weigert‑hematoxylin to highlight elastic lamellae. Examine thoracic aorta sections at 40× magnification and carotid/femoral sections at 100× under a Leica DM4 B microscope; capture images with a Leica MC170 HD camera.

steps.title: Prepare cryosections for collagen analysis
steps.instruction: Embed fresh arterial segments in Tissue‑Tek O.C.T. (Sakura®), snap‑freeze in liquid nitrogen, and cut 5 µm cryosections with a cryostat. Stain sections with 0.1 % (w/v) Picrosirius Red solution.

steps.title: Image and quantify collagen deposition
steps.instruction: Capture bright‑field images of each stained section at 400× magnification using an Olympus Bx43‑SC30 microscope. For each artery, analyse four equally sized areas per animal with ImageJ to obtain the percentage of collagen‑positive area. Perform the analysis blinded to group identity.

steps.title: Score elastin fiber disarray
steps.instruction: Using the Weigert‑hematoxylin stained sections (400×), evaluate three microscopic fields per rat and assign a disarray score (1‑4): 1 = ≤ 25 % disrupted, 2 = 26‑50 % disrupted, 3 = 56‑75 % disrupted, 4 = ≥ 76 % disrupted. Record mean scores for each age group.

steps.title: Measure blood pressure in hypertensive rats (Study 3)
steps.instruction: After PWV measurement, perform carotid catheterisation surgery on six 5‑month‑old Wistar rats and six age‑matched male spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR). Twenty‑four hours later, record systolic arterial pressure (SAP) as described in reference [19].

steps.title: Record and compare PWV and SAP values
steps.instruction: Document PWV and SAP for each animal. Expected mean values: young Wistar PWV ≈ 3.63 ± 0.08 m s⁻¹, adult PWV ≈ 4.86 ± 0.15 m s⁻¹, old PWV ≈ 6.21 ± 0.32 m s⁻¹; transit times 17.65 ± 0.40 ms, 21.9 ± 0.66 ms, 18.93 ± 0.93 ms; probe distances 6.38 ± 0.13 cm, 10.5 ± 0.11 cm, 11.5 ± 0.13 cm. Body weights: young ≈ 81 ± 1.83 g, adult ≈ 424 ± 10.89 g, old ≈ 566 ± 15.06 g. In Study 3, SHR SAP = 224 ± 13 mmHg vs Wistar = 126 ± 2 mmHg; SHR PWV = 7.98 ± 0.85 m s⁻¹ vs Wistar = 4.64 ± 0.17 m s⁻¹. Correlation PWV vs SAP: r = 0.923, p < 0.0001.
